questions.q: Why does starting from a real business question work better than memorizing an abstract table list?
options: Business questions never require more than one table
Oracle Fusion has no documentation for business questions
It doesn't — abstract memorization is always more effective
It forces you to identify a driving table and trace outward only as far as the question requires, learning tables with a reason attached
questions.explain: Starting from a concrete question anchors the tables you learn to a reason you'll remember, rather than memorizing names in isolation.

questions.q: What is the recommended first step in the repeatable mapping process?
options: Skip documentation entirely and guess from column names
Map every module in the application simultaneously
Pick one module at a time, starting with whichever you'll use first
Memorize every column on every table before doing anything else
questions.explain: The process recommends focusing on one module at a time rather than trying to map everything simultaneously.

questions.q: What should a durable personal note on a table actually contain?
options: The table name, primary key, one line on what a row represents, and the foreign keys relevant to your question
Nothing — notes are discouraged in favor of memorization
Only the table's creation date
Every single column, copied in full from the documentation
questions.explain: A short note — name, key, meaning, relevant foreign keys — is a durable "why it connects" layer on top of Oracle's own documentation, not a duplicate of it.

questions.q: How can OTBI subject areas help validate a hand-built data map?
options: They can't — OTBI is unrelated to the underlying tables
Subject areas are built on views over the same base tables, so how they group fields can hint at real underlying relationships
OTBI subject areas replace the need for any table documentation
OTBI only works with Receivables data
questions.explain: Because OTBI subject areas sit on views over the same base tables, their field groupings can serve as a sanity check on relationships traced by hand.

questions.q: Why is confirming a foreign-key relationship against documented column descriptions better than guessing from column names?
options: Documentation is never accurate for Oracle Fusion
Foreign keys are never documented anywhere
Column names are always sufficient on their own
Similarly-named columns can carry subtly different meanings across tables, so the documented description resolves ambiguity reliably
questions.explain: This reinforces lesson 3's core habit: read the documented description rather than assuming a column's meaning from its name alone.
